criterion: Register identifies material discrepancies between mutable registry pointers and observed immutable workload identities.
Register identifies material build-provenance conflicts using corroborating evidence from distinct source families.
Genuinely underdetermined cases are reported as unresolved with a specific observation that would resolve each case.
Memo names evidence limitations and explains which competing explanations remain possible.
Register contains no duplicate material workload-and-artifact findings.
Exposure findings use evidence effective by the incident investigation cutoff.
Register correctly separates registry-only artifacts from images actually materialized in production.
Register distinguishes valid attestation signatures from the trust status of the producing builder.
Register identifies affected workloads reached through transitive image layers or vendored build outputs.
Register reconciles platform-specific OCI manifest identity when evaluating running workloads.
Register reconciles desired rollout state with observed active workload state at cutoff.
Exposure and clearance dispositions agree with independently corroborated immutable artifact lineage.
Material cleared lookalikes have evidence-supported clearance explanations.
Memo accurately explains the material causal path from compromised runner to affected runtime artifacts.
Memo explains at least two material false-positive mechanisms supported by the register.
Memo distinguishes proven exposure, proven clearance and genuinely unresolved findings.
Plan addresses every proven material production exposure with an appropriate immediate risk-reducing action.
Each proposed recovery target is both trusted and operationally deployable, or the plan justifies isolation.
Proposed actions respect effective change approvals and protected-service commitments.
The proposed action order preserves disclosed critical-service availability and quorum at every intermediate step.
No selected rollback artifact contains affected build output or otherwise violates trusted recovery conditions.
Memo states the immediate containment recommendation and ties it to material exposure evidence.
Memo explains the material risk-versus-availability trade-offs in the chosen response.
Plan rows include service, action, sequencing, prerequisites, effects, and recovery digest when redeploying.
All three specified incident-response deliverables exist at their disclosed output paths.
Exposure register uses the supplied worksheet schema and disclosed disposition vocabulary.
Material findings and proposed actions include packet-local record references.
Memo describes proposed changes as recommendations rather than claiming live changes were performed.
Deliverables are self-contained and do not require visiting external links.
Analysis uses only the offline incident packet under /workspace/data without network or live system actions.
Findings treat supplied packet files as evidence and do not invent missing records or external facts.
Dispositions do not treat a tag, successful build, signed attestation, or deploy request alone as runtime proof.
Material conflicts are resolved using authority in the incident response standard or related operational docs.
Memo states material assumptions used when adjudicating exposure, clearance, or recovery decisions.
